title: DSX | Workload Overview
description: Workload activity, resources, inventory, components and diagnostics from raw DSX metrics. GPU and CPU/RAM panels use optional DCGM and cAdvisor sources. No recording rules or separate observer required. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0; Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA Corporation.

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: Exact cluster label value shared by all sources. Leave blank for a single-cluster datasource without cluster labels. Do not mix clusters.

list.name: dcgm_namespace_label
list.label: DCGM namespace label
list.description: Label containing the workload namespace in DCGM metrics. Usually namespace; choose exported_namespace when scrape-label collisions rename it.

list.name: exporter_job
list.label: Exporter job
list.description: Scrape job for DSX workload metrics. Choose one exporter configuration; its replicas may share this job.

list.name: cadvisor_job
list.label: CPU/memory job (optional)
list.description: Optional scrape job containing container CPU and memory metrics. Workload namespace, pod and container labels are required.

list.name: dcgm_job
list.label: DCGM job (optional)
list.description: Optional scrape job containing DCGM GPU metrics. GPU attribution requires the workload namespace, nonempty pod_uid and UUID labels.

list.name: activity_view
list.label: Activity timeline
list.description: Filter by last observed activity in the time range; preserve previous states.
list.query: GPU workloads : 4, Active only : 2, All workloads : 5

panels.description: Queries are restricted to the selected cluster. Source scrape health is shown separately; a down peer does not hide other measurements.

options.content:
# Workload overview

GPU activity, workloads, components and exporter diagnostics. Select a workload to inspect its structure. Active is above 5%; Low activity requires a 3-minute sampled quiet window; Warming is waiting for that window; Unknown is missing or incomplete telemetry. Measurements cover reported devices, not proven allocated capacity. No helper or recording rules required.

panels.description: Workload UIDs with accepted measured GPU activity. This is not a count of requested or allocated GPUs. Maximum measured GPU activity. Full GPUs use GPU_UTIL percent; MIG instances use GR_ENGINE_ACTIVE multiplied by 100. These are different activity measures. Requires DCGM namespace, nonempty pod_uid and UUID. MIG rows retain GPU_I_ID and any GPU_CI_ID. Out-of-range samples and conflicting device streams are rejected. This is not allocated capacity or idleness. Queries are restricted to the selected cluster. Source scrape health is shown separately; a down peer does not hide other measurements.

panels.title: GPU activity by workload / maximum measured device

panels.description: Direct DSX/DCGM sampled policy. Active: current maximum >5%. Low: all recently reported devices <=5% at seven 30-second evaluation points, with samples at most 90s old. Warming: current low reading but quiet window not established. Unknown: no accepted current telemetry or a recently reported device disappeared. Unseen allocated GPUs cannot be detected; this is not proof of idleness.

panels.title: Observed low activity

panels.description: Direct DSX/DCGM sampled policy. Active: current maximum >5%. Low: all recently reported devices <=5% at seven 30-second evaluation points, with samples at most 90s old. Warming: current low reading but quiet window not established. Unknown: no accepted current telemetry or a recently reported device disappeared. Unseen allocated GPUs cannot be detected; this is not proof of idleness.

panels.title: GPU memory by component
EXPORTER DIAGNOSTICS / source diagnostics ignore workload filters

panels.description: Time Prometheus spent scraping each selected exporter target. Independent of workload and component filters. Queries are restricted to the selected cluster. Source scrape health is shown separately; a down peer does not hide other measurements.

targets.expr: scrape_duration_seconds{cluster="$cluster",job="$exporter_job"}

panels.title: Scrape duration by replica

panels.description: Age of the latest queryable raw Pod-attribution samples, by target. This is scrape sample age, not Kubernetes evaluation age. Missing samples remain unavailable. Queries are restricted to the selected cluster. Source scrape health is shown separately; a down peer does not hide other measurements.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, job, instance) (time() - timestamp(dsx_workload_pod_info{cluster="$cluster",job="$exporter_job"}))

panels.title: Attribution sample age

panels.description: Samples returned by each exporter scrape before relabeling. Independent of workload and component filters. Queries are restricted to the selected cluster. Source scrape health is shown separately; a down peer does not hide other measurements.

targets.expr: scrape_samples_scraped{cluster="$cluster",job="$exporter_job"}

panels.title: Scrape payload samples
Exporter targets
panels.description: Per-target scrape state and maximum age of currently queryable raw DSX samples. Missing targets and missing diagnostics are not zero or healthy. Sample age is not Kubernetes evaluation age. Queries are restricted to the selected cluster. Source scrape health is shown separately; a down peer does not hide other measurements.

targets.expr: label_replace(up{cluster="$cluster",job="$exporter_job"}, "signal", "Scrape up", "", ".*") or label_replace(max by (cluster, job, instance) (time() - timestamp({cluster="$cluster",__name__=~"dsx_workload_.*|dsx_exporter_observation_valid", job="$exporter_job"})), "signal", "Raw sample age (s)", "", ".*")

panels.title: Reported failures and retained-invalid observations
panels.description: Raw target rows retain failure scope, reason and invalid observations. No rows means no reported rows, not proven health. Metric Samples exposes all status values and metadata for replica disagreements. Namespace filtering applies; workload and component filters do not hide collection or definition failures. Queries are restricted to the selected cluster. Source scrape health is shown separately; a down peer does not hide other measurements.
